polishes.said: I'm in office right now at the end of the day.
polishes.natural: I'm at the office right now at the end of the day.
polishes.why: In natural English, we say 'at the office' (or 'in the office' with the definite article). In Italian, 'in ufficio' lacks an article, which makes this a very natural instinct to gently polish!

polishes.said: My company requested courses for improve my English.
polishes.natural: My company requested courses to improve my English.
polishes.why: When expressing purpose or reason for an action, English uses the full infinitive ('to improve') rather than 'for + base verb'. You can also say 'for improving', but 'to improve' is most elegant.

polishes.said: You can use it to do the wine.
polishes.natural: You can use them to make wine.
polishes.why: Grapes are plural ('them'), and in English we 'make wine' or 'produce wine' rather than 'do the wine' (a direct translation of Italian 'fare il vino').

polishes.said: This is a typical first plate with mushroom—risotto.
polishes.natural: This is a typical first course with mushrooms—risotto.
polishes.why: In Italian dining, 'primo piatto' is translated into English as 'first course' or 'starter'. Also, we pluralize 'mushrooms' when used as an ingredient.

polishes.said: No, I don't drink the wines.
polishes.why: When talking about beverages in general, we omit the article 'the' and treat wine as an uncountable noun: 'I don't drink wine' or 'I'm not a wine drinker'.

polishes.said: I had some parents that are twins.
polishes.natural: I have some relatives who are twins.
polishes.why: A classic Italian false friend! Italian 'parenti' means 'relatives' or 'extended family'. In English, 'parents' strictly means your mother and father (genitori).

quiz.q: 1. When you weigh the benefit of high quality against a much higher financial cost, you are evaluating a ________.
quiz.explain: 'Trade-off' (05:52) refers to balancing two desirable qualities where gaining one means sacrificing another.

quiz.q: 2. In English, how should an Italian speaker describe their aunts, uncles, and cousins to avoid the 'parenti' false friend?
quiz.explain: 'Relatives' (23:51) refers to extended family members; 'parents' in English strictly means mother and father (genitori).

quiz.q: 3. When an engineer is added to an ongoing email thread so they receive every update, they are kept ________.
quiz.explain: Being 'in the loop' (13:48) means being included in the flow of information and updates.

quiz.q: 4. In the tabletop game 7 Wonders, players select one card and pass the remaining hand to their neighbor. This mechanism is called ________.
quiz.explain: 'Card drafting' (33:49) is the tabletop mechanic where players choose cards from a rotating communal hand.

quiz.q: 5. What is the natural English equivalent of the Italian dining term 'il primo' (such as mushroom risotto)?
quiz.explain: In English dining (17:40), 'primo piatto' translates naturally to 'first course' or 'starter'.

quiz.q: 6. When Louie tried to stay completely silent during the Werewolf / Lupus in Tabula game but talked anyway, his effort was ________.
quiz.explain: 'To no avail' (39:22) means without success or positive result despite earnest trying.
